**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification right exercisable by Garman against Sparkling:

- **Section 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the planner's most likely home for a licence-compliance audit — runs from limb (a) through limb (g) as pure use covenants (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau) with no accompanying right for Garman to verify compliance, count copies, or access Sparkling systems.
- **Section 20 (General Matters)** contains only time-of-essence and notice mechanics.
- Text searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "premises", "remote" and "records" surface no audit-type right binding us.
- The single examination right in the document runs **in our favour**: Section 16 escrow permits Sparkling, itself or via independent experts, to examine and test the deposited materials for Garman's compliance.

Because there is no audit right against the Customer at all, there is nothing that could exceed the preferred limits on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access — the position is better than preferred. Consistent with the rule's direction (audits *against* Customer), the absence benefits us, so I have not proposed inserting an audit framework; doing so would manufacture an exposure we do not currently carry.
